newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DUVAL LEADS HOUSTON OPEN BY ONE AT MIDWAY POINT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUVAL LEADS HOUSTON OPEN BY ONE AT MIDWAY POINT.

text.p: David Duval, a non-winner in four-plus years on the U.S. PGA Tour, was halfway to the winners' circle after firing a one-under-par 71 on Friday for a one stroke lead at the midway point of the 50th Houston Open.
Duval, the overnight leader after a blistering first-round 65, stood at seven-under 136 after 36 holes -- one shot ahead of Australian Craig Parry, who fired a 66, and David Ogrin, who carded a 68.
Fred Couples and Jerry Kelly were another shot off the pace at 138.
"It was harder to score today because the winds were swirling more and the greens were pretty bumpy," Duval said. "It was hard to judge the putts."

Duval opened on the 10th hole with a bogey, but parred the next nine holes. He suffered another setback on the par-4 second hole, but recovered with birdies on three, five and seven to reach one-under for the round.
While looking for his first victory, Duval has recorded six second place finishes over the last two seasons.
He said he was not letting the pressure to win get to him, especially with eight golfers within four shots of the lead.
"I'm not worried about winning on tour. I'm just going to relax and let it happen," Duval said.
Parry seems to thrive in Texas and posted the low round of the day Friday with seven birdies and just one bogey.
He finished second at the Byron Nelson Classic in Dallas last year and had a runner-up finish at the 1995 Colonial in Fort Worth.
"These courses are more suited to my game," Parry said of the Texas events.
"The ball bounces and rolls more here, like the European courses."
